subject: LiveChat: severe tail-latency surge during end-of-day peak — urgent
messages:
From: Alex Romero <alex@boxline.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, support@boxline.ai
Date: Thu, 09 May 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Live chat tail latency spike — SSE disconnects at 17:05 PDT

Laura —

Having an urgent issue on our side during yesterday's end-of-day ramp (approx 17:00-17:20 PDT). Our operators saw a big jump in 95/99 latency for streaming chat: p95 jumped from ~220ms to ~2.1s and p99 spiked to ~6.8s. Several users reported truncated streaming messages and we saw repeated SSE reconnects (many with 502/503).

Attached is a small trace capture (boxline_sse_traces_20280509.log) and a Grafana snapshot (attached) showing the latency curve. We are on your hosted API region us-west-2, model redwood-chat-v2 (default routing). This week we hit a heavier than normal traffic burst due to a marketing promo; peak concurrent streams around 1,700.

Can you confirm whether anything changed on Redwood's side (deploys, autoscaler config, model variant flips) around 17:00 PDT? We need a temp mitigation — even a fallback to poll-based responses would keep the UX usable while you triage.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Romero
Head of Integrations, Boxline
alex@boxline.ai

Forwarding Boxline report — high priority customer (BOX-2024-128). Key points: p95->~2s, p99->~6-7s, SSE reconnects, occurred ~17:00 PDT, ~1,700 concurrent streams. They attached traces and a dashboard snapshot.

Immediate ask:
- Rishi/Dylan: please triage on-call and confirm whether any autoscaler or routing changes happened around that window. Check model-variant routing (did we fall back to a slower quantized variant?), queue/backpressure metrics, and the streaming runtime thread/IO saturation.

If we can't stabilize in 30–45m, request an exec sync with CTO and VP Eng. Attachments from customer are included.

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Success (Escalations), Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: sean.gallagher@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 09 May 2028 10:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Live chat tail latency spike — SSE disconnects at 17:05 PDT

Triage update (initial):
- No user-facing deploys recorded at 16:30–17:30 PDT.
- Autoscaler: saw high churn on the dedicated streaming pool in us-west-2 starting ~16:55; scale events every ~45s (thrash). Root suspect: a recent config change to the continuous batching threshold (we lowered the min-batch-delay to 5ms last week for throughput gains) combined with an unusual sequence length distribution from Boxline. That produced a burst of small batches that stressed the runqueue and increased latency for tail requests.
- Model routing: traffic stayed on redwood-chat-v2, but we did see fallback attempts to redwood-chat-v2-quant64 for some large requests — those requests showed higher token latency.

Immediate mitigations applied (10:40 PDT):
1) Temporarily raised min-batch-delay from 5ms -> 20ms for the streaming pool serving Boxline to reduce thrash (patch: eng_patch_stream_config.diff attached).
2) Pinned Boxline traffic to non-quant variant for the next 4 hours to avoid slower fallback.
3) Increased max-pool-size by +20% to absorb burst traffic.

Early results: p95 improved from ~2s -> ~450ms within ~6 minutes; p99 trending down but still elevated (~1.6s). We'll keep monitoring.

Next steps:
- Run a targeted load replay against their traffic shape to reproduce the pattern.
- Evaluate altering autoscaler cooldown logic to prevent thrash when batch distribution is high-variance.
- If p99 doesn't normalize within 2 hours, we should consider a short maintenance window to fully revert the batching change.

Rishi
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Romero <alex@boxline.ai>
Cc: support@boxline.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 09 May 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Live chat tail latency spike — SSE disconnects at 17:05 PDT

Alex —

Thanks for the traces and patience. Rishi's team found autoscaler thrash tied to a change in batching config; we've applied short-term mitigations: increased batch delay and pinned your traffic to the non-quant variant. Early telemetry shows p95 down to ~450ms and p99 improving but not fully restored.

Short-term customer-facing options you can enable now (low friction):
- Switch to a polling fallback (non-streaming responses) for high-concurrency sessions — we can toggle this for your account immediately and it will avoid SSE reconnection surface area.
- Reduce max concurrent streams per session from 50 -> 20 (limits quick bursts).

If you'd like us to toggle either, tell me which and we will make the change now. Apologies for the disruption during your promo window — we know this is bad timing.

Laura
Head of Customer Success (Escalations), Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 10 May 2028 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec summary: Boxline livechat tail-latency incident (next 48h asks)

Quick summary for execs: Boxline (BOX-2024-128) experienced a severe p95/p99 spike for the streaming chat endpoint during an end-of-day traffic surge on 2028-05-09 ~17:00 PDT. Root cause (initial): interaction between a recent batching min-delay reduction and a high-variance traffic shape that caused autoscaler thrash and delayed runqueue processing — led to SSE reconnects and increased token tail latency.

Immediate actions taken:
- Raised batching min-delay for Boxline's streaming pool (+ patched config).
- Pinned traffic off quantized fallback for 4h.
- Increased pool capacity +20%.
- Customer offered polling fallback and concurrency limit options (awaiting decision).

Asks:
1) Product/ENG: schedule a rollback safety review for the batching change and add a canary/monitor gate that triggers autoscaler cooldown safeguards when batch variance > threshold. Owner: Rishi.
2) Sales/CS: coordinate with Boxline on a 2-hour maintenance window tonight if p99 plateaus. Owner: Laura/Sean.
3) Ops: run a replay test of Boxline traffic shape against us-west-2 streaming pool and produce a short RCA doc with repro steps and metrics. Owner: Dylan.

I'd like a short exec sync (15–20m) if p99 remains above 1.2s by EOD PDT. Leaving notes and links here: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/streams/livechat?from=now-2h&to=now and incident doc https://docs.redwood.internal/incidents/BOXLINE-2028-05-09.

Laura
